title: Phawar of Demeanor and Gait (Akor Iaid Akor Ieng)
khasi_title: Akor Iaid Akor Ieng Ha Ka Rukom Rwai Phawar
cultural_context: The classical opening rhyming chant (Rwai Phawar) of Radhon Singh Berry's monumental 1902 work 'Ka Jingsneng Tymmen', instructing youth on dignified physical comportment.

khasi: Haba phi iaid ha ka lynti,
Wat iaid khia kti khia kjat shuh;
Wat peit suh khmat sha pnah bneng,
Iaid beit, iaid suk da ka akor;
Ka rukom iaid ka pynpaw bha,
Ia ka dohnud ba don ha poh;
Uba iaid da ka burom briew
U ioh ka nam kaba tyngshain.
english: Whenever your footsteps walk the road,
Tread not heavily with boisterous gait;
Cast not haughty eyes toward the clouds,
Walk direct and peacefully with upright decorum;
The manner of one's stride clearly reveals
The inner spirit that dwells within;
He who walks with human dignity
Earns an honorable name that shines.

khasi: Wat ksaid ha ling, wat khie bitar,
Wat kren da ka ktien ba pait dohnud;
Ki tymmen ki peit da ka jingstad,
Ban sneng ban bthah ia la ki khun;
Ka akor babha dei ka spah ksiar,
Haduh ba sngi jong ngi kan sep
To ngin bat skhem ia kane ka nia.
english: Fume not within the hearth, rise not in wrath,
Utter no harsh word that fractures the soul;
The elders observe with deep wisdom,
To counsel and guide their children;
Good character is true treasure of gold,
Cherished by all the Seven Huts;
Until the final sun of our life shall set
Let us cling steadfastly to this truth.
